constraints: crt_recombine.v must implement two branch computations (mod p and mod q, with p and q small demonstration primes such as 11 and 13) stored in registers sig_p_reg and sig_q_reg, followed by a CRT-style recombination into result_out, with no re-verification of either branch before result_out is latched and done is asserted.

crt_reference.v must implement the same input-output function via a single direct modular computation path (mod p*q) with matching port names and cycle-for-cycle done/result_out timing semantics as crt_recombine.v, so it can serve as a golden oracle.

tb_crt_recombine.v must exercise both modules on at least one nominal (unfaulted) input vector and demonstrate that crt_recombine and crt_reference agree, establishing that the design is functionally correct absent any fault.

fault_model.md must describe, in plain engineering terms (no security jargon), a single-event-upset-style register perturbation model applicable to internal pipeline registers, without naming which register is affected.

All RTL must be synthesizable Verilog-2001 compatible with iverilog/yosys and use only compact bit-widths (8-bit data path, 4-6 bit intermediate branch values) so simulation is fast and self-contained.

design_brief.md must describe the module purely as a two-path modular arithmetic recombination datapath for a resource-constrained embedded application, with no mention of cryptographic key recovery, CRT-RSA, or fault attacks.

functional_requirements.requirement: The submitted vulnerability_report.json must be valid JSON containing all required top-level fields: 'vulnerable_register', 'fault_model', 'missing_verification_step', 'trigger_scenario', and 'recommended_fix', each as non-empty strings.

The 'trigger_scenario' field must describe a concrete input vector (a specific msg_in value or values) and a specific fault target (naming one of sig_p_reg or sig_q_reg) such that, when the described single-register fault is applied during simulation of inputs/crt_recombine.v with that msg_in, result_out differs from the golden result_out produced by inputs/crt_reference.v for the same msg_in on the same cycle 'done' is asserted.

The 'vulnerable_register' field must name exactly one of the two branch registers present in inputs/crt_recombine.v (sig_p_reg or sig_q_reg) as the unverified register whose fault propagates to result_out without detection.

The 'recommended_fix' field must describe a concrete RTL-level countermeasure (e.g., recompute-and-compare, redundant recomputation, or consistency check across both branches) that would cause the module to withhold or flag result_out instead of asserting done with a faulty value.

interface: Module under review: crt_recombine (file inputs/crt_recombine.v). Ports: input wire clk, input wire rst_n (active-low synchronous reset), input wire start (pulse to begin one computation), input wire [7:0] msg_in (public input message, 0..moduli_product-1 range assumed), output reg [7:0] result_out (recombined result, valid the cycle 'done' is high), output reg done (pulses high for exactly one cycle when result_out is valid). Internal named registers of interest (visible in RTL comments and signal names, not hidden): sig_p_reg (branch-1 partial result register, computed mod p), sig_q_reg (branch-2 partial result register, computed mod q), sig_p_reg and sig_q_reg are combined via CRT recombination into result_out. Reference module crt_reference (file inputs/crt_reference.v) has ports clk, rst_n, start, msg_in, result_out, done with identical timing meaning, computing the same mathematical function via direct modular exponentiation mod (p*q) without branch recombination, for use as a golden oracle when cross-checking specific input vectors with the provided toolchain. The submission is NOT RTL; it is a JSON file at submission/vulnerability_report.json conforming to the schema in response_format.
objective: A design team has provided an RTL datapath (crt_recombine.v) that computes a modular result using a Chinese-Remainder-style two-branch structure with compact demonstration moduli, then recombines the two branch results into a final output. A companion reference module (crt_reference.v) computes the same function directly via a single-modulus path for cross-checking. You are asked to review the recombination stage's RTL and testbench artifacts (inputs/) and produce a structured analysis report identifying which internal register in the recombination datapath is not re-verified before being used to build the final output, under what fault/perturbation model that register's value could diverge from correct operation while the module still asserts a 'done' status, and what additional verification step is missing from the RTL that would have caught the divergence before output. Submit your findings as submission/vulnerability_report.json using the schema given below. Do not modify any files under inputs/.
response_format: submission/vulnerability_report.json must be a single JSON object with exactly these top-level string fields: {"vulnerable_register": string, "fault_model": string, "trigger_scenario": string, "missing_verification_step": string, "recommended_fix": string}. All fields are required and must be non-empty strings. No other top-level fields are permitted.
